hero.headline: Humane Society of the Treasure Coast uses Stuart thrift stores for animal care during Palm City shelter renovations
hero.teaser: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is using its two thrift stores to keep animal care going during a major renovation of its shelter in Palm City.
hero.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is relying on its two thrift stores to maintain animal care operations while undergoing major renovations at its Palm City shelter. The nonprofit started construction on its adoption, customer service, and intake areas earlier this year, which forced the organization to find creative solutions for housing its animals. According to spokesperson Sarah Fisher, many of the shelter's cats have been temporarily moved to the thrift store locations. Fisher emphasized how important this transition has been, noting that with their shelter cages unavailable during construction, the stores have provided essential space for the animals.

The thrift stores are now serving dual purposes for the organization. Senior Manager Kelly Ellis explained that customers shopping for unique items can also browse adoptable cats while visiting either location. This approach keeps the animals visible to potential adopters while freeing up much-needed space at the main facility. Ellis stressed that every purchase made at the thrift stores directly supports the animals in their care. The organization welcomes donations of gently used goods, which shoppers can drop off while exploring the merchandise and meeting available pets.

While the stores house some animals during construction, the Humane Society is also actively seeking temporary foster homes for other animals. This two-pronged approach allows the organization to care for its full population while the renovation project continues. The strategy demonstrates how animal shelters can adapt when buildings require upgrades, maintaining both operations and community connections during challenging transitions.

The Humane Society's thrift stores are located at 3302 SE Federal Highway in Stuart and 1099 NW 21st Street in Stuart. For more information about store hours and guidelines for donating items, visit hstc1.org.

cards.headline: Lawsuit challenges Florida property tax amendment ballot language as misleading
cards.teaser: A voter advocacy group and two registered voters filed a lawsuit Thursday in Leon County challenging the ballot language for the property tax amendment Florida .
cards.body:
A voter advocacy group and two registered voters filed a lawsuit Thursday in Leon County challenging the ballot language for a property tax amendment Florida lawmakers approved for the November 2026 General Election ballot. The complaint argues the ballot language is "biased" and "misleading," accusing lawmakers of using campaign-style phrases like "Save Our Homes From Excessive Property Taxes," "protecting small businesses" and "ensuring fairness." The plaintiffs say the summary overstates the proposal by suggesting it guarantees funding for core services, fully eliminates non-school homestead taxes and immediately exempts the first $250,000 of a home's value, when the filing argues the initial exemption would be $150,000 in 2027. The lawsuit asks a judge to declare the wording unconstitutional and order Attorney General James Uthmeier to rewrite it within 10 days.

Attorney Jamie Cole, who represents the plaintiffs, said a ballot amendment is supposed to be fair, neutral and accurate. Cole successfully challenged a similar property tax amendment in 2007 when a judge found the ballot language for a proposed Super Exemption misleading and ordered the measure removed from the ballot. On June 2, lawmakers passed legislation to raise the homestead exemption to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028 and create a framework for full exemption over time. The amendment will require approval from at least 60 percent of voters to become law.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie police drone locates missing autistic woman on first day of new program
cards.teaser: Port St.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie's new Drone as First Responder program proved its value on its first day of testing Wednesday, completing 17 missions. The most significant involved locating a missing autistic female who was walking through a wooded area near a canal bank. A DFR drone was remotely deployed and arrived at the scene before responding officers, quickly locating both the missing female and the reporting party. Drone operators maintained visual contact and directed responding officers to their exact location, allowing officers to safely reunite the female with her family. Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said the successful location of the vulnerable autistic female near a canal before officers arrived demonstrates the tremendous value this technology brings to the community.

The DFR program integrates directly with Port St. Lucie's computer-aided dispatch system, allowing trained personnel to remotely deploy drones from the police department. Drones can reach calls within seconds, with the longest travel time within the coverage area approximately four minutes. Each drone has an average flight time of 25 to 35 minutes depending on weather conditions. On Wednesday, the drones also responded to a burglary in progress where they provided aerial overwatch, a domestic violence investigation where they located a suspect in a backyard, and multiple disturbance calls involving groups of minors. Three drone docks are currently active during testing and evaluation, with plans for six docks throughout Port St. Lucie once fully operational. The DFR team consists of 12 specially trained officers.

cards.headline: Wrongful death lawsuit filed in St. Lucie County after fatal Florida Turnpike crash that killed three
cards.teaser: The lawsuit names the truck driver, White Hawk Carriers Inc., freight broker C.H. Robinson, and a company manager as defendants in the Aug. 12, 2025 crash near Mile Marker 171.
cards.body:
A wrongful death lawsuit was filed Thursday months after a fatal crash on Florida's Turnpike that killed three people when a semi-truck driver made an illegal U-turn in St. Lucie County. The lawsuit, filed by an attorney representing the estate of victim Faniola Joseph, names multiple defendants including truck driver Harjinder Singh, trucking company White Hawk Carriers Inc., freight broker C.H. Robinson, and company manager Harpreet Singh. On Aug. 12, 2025, at approximately 2:57 p.m., Harjinder Singh attempted an illegal U-turn through a median crossover on Florida's Turnpike near Mile Marker 171. The crossover was clearly marked "U-TURN OFFICIAL USE ONLY," according to court documents. The 53-foot trailer swung across and completely blocked all northbound travel lanes. A minivan driven by Herby Dufresne, carrying passengers Rodrigue Dor and Faniola Joseph, struck the left side of the trailer in what the complaint describes as "a classic and fatal underride crash." All three occupants were killed, with Joseph pronounced dead at the scene.

The lawsuit alleges White Hawk Carriers had a documented unsafe federal safety record before C.H. Robinson selected the company to transport the load. The complaint includes a prior reportable crash on approximately Dec. 9, 2024, multiple roadside inspection citations for unsafe driving violations including speeding and improper lane changes, repeated hours-of-service violations with falsified duty status records, and vehicle defects including brake problems and air-brake leaks. C.H. Robinson, one of the largest transportation brokers in the United States with headquarters in Eden Prairie, Minnesota, is named as a defendant. The lawsuit also names Harpreet Singh, a White Hawk Carriers manager, individually, alleging he failed to adequately investigate the truck driver's immigration status, work authorization, and English proficiency before hiring. The lawsuit seeks damages exceeding $75,000 under Florida's Wrongful Death Act.

cards.headline: Lake Worth man shoots at ex-girlfriend in Boynton Beach parking lot before being shot in chest
cards.teaser: Frisner St. Cyr, 44, faces attempted first-degree murder charges after shooting at his ex-girlfriend and her friend near an LA Fitness gym on Wednesday evening.
cards.body:
A Lake Worth man is hospitalized in critical condition after shooting at his ex-girlfriend and her friend in a parking lot at 2244 N. Congress Ave. in Boynton Beach on Wednesday evening before one of the victims returned fire, striking him in the chest. Frisner St. Cyr, 44, faces multiple felony charges including attempted first-degree murder with a firearm. Police responded to reports of shots fired around 6:55 p.m. Wednesday in the parking lot near an LA Fitness gym.

According to an arrest report, St. Cyr drove his black Cadillac to the parking lot where his ex-girlfriend worked and used the vehicle to block her friend's car. St. Cyr exited his vehicle with a firearm and immediately began shooting at both victims, firing multiple rounds through the Honda's windshield. Both victims fled on foot as St. Cyr pursued them through the parking lot, continuing to fire shots. During the chase, one of the victims returned fire, striking St. Cyr once in the chest. Boynton Beach Fire Rescue transported St. Cyr to Delray Medical Center. St. Cyr faces charges of attempted first-degree murder with a firearm, shooting into an occupied vehicle, aggravated assault with a deadly weapon and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. The two victims were not physically injured in the shooting.

cards.headline: Hundreds of fish found dead in Port St. Lucie community after city algae treatment
cards.teaser: Dead fish were floating in the Sawgrass Lakes community in Port St. Lucie on Thursday after the city hired a vendor to treat the water for toxic algae earlier in the week.
cards.body:
Dead fish were found floating in the Sawgrass Lakes community on Thursday morning after the city of Port St. Lucie treated the water for toxic algae on Tuesday and Wednesday. The city hired SOLitude to perform the treatment. Neighbors shared videos of hundreds of dead fish in their backyards, with resident Jim Herbert describing "hundreds and hundreds of fish here, hundreds and hundreds of those little ones just gulping the air." Experts told WPTV that high heat combined with algae treatment can make water uninhabitable for aquatic life. On Thursday, crews removed the dead fish and tested oxygen levels in the water.

Scott Samples with the city of Port St. Lucie said the city has been working with neighbors and other cities and counties to find solutions. Jim Moir, executive director of the Indian Riverkeeper, recommended the city pursue more natural approaches, including planting aquatic vegetation, reducing fertilizer use, and removing sediment that fuels algae growth. Moir stated, "We're going to end up in a cycle that we can't break unless we go back to square one and start with a natural remediation." Resident Jim Herbert noted this was at least the second fish die-off since he has lived in the neighborhood. Neighbor Jerry Cook said he does not think the issue is "an overnight fix" or "a couple months fix," but rather "a few years fix."

cards.teaser: Hundreds of soccer fans filled Florida Atlantic University stadium in Boca Raton Thursday to watch Curaçao hold a training session ahead of the team's first-eve.
cards.body:
Hundreds of soccer fans gathered at Florida Atlantic University stadium in Boca Raton on Thursday, waving jerseys and flags to witness Curaçao's training session ahead of the team's historic first-ever World Cup appearance this weekend. Goalkeeper Eloy Room told WPTV the large turnout energized the squad. "Really joyful to see that so many people showed up today — it gives us energy. hero.headline: Wellington posts highest rental costs in Palm Beach County at $2,850 for one bedroom
hero.teaser: Wellington residents face the highest rental costs in Palm Beach County, with Fair Market Rent reaching nearly $2,850 for a one-bedroom apartment, according to new 2026 data from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
hero.body:
Wellington residents are experiencing the steepest rental prices in Palm Beach County, with new federal data showing one-bedroom apartments averaging nearly $2,850 monthly. The ZIP code 33449 in Wellington recorded the county's highest Fair Market Rent rates, with four-bedroom homes surpassing $5,080 per month, according to 2026 data from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. These figures stand in sharp contrast to Belle Glade, which offers the county's most affordable housing options at $890 for comparable four-bedroom units.

The rising costs are reshaping how residents navigate the local market. Luis Rivera, who receives Section 8 housing assistance in Palm Beach County, said the situation has become increasingly difficult. "You have to budget — there's no way out of it," he explained, noting that he regularly sees rental listings exceeding two to three thousand dollars for substandard neighborhoods. "When I first came down here rent prices were normal. And now it's like they're pushing us out," he added. The market's affordability challenges have also affected job seekers like Joanne Bromfield, who relocated from Tampa after a 12-year education career to pursue real estate opportunities. She was unprepared for the rental market's demands. "We literally just walked away from signing a lease like 5 minutes ago," she said. "Expensive, very expensive."

Real estate broker Talbot Sutter, president of Sutter and Nugent Real Estate, attributes Wellington's premium pricing to its community advantages. "A lot of it has to do with school districts, especially Wellington. They have like top A-rated schools, lifestyle, and they have so many aspects from equestrian to outdoor activities," Sutter said. His high-end clientele often includes executives relocating from New York City who rent luxury properties before committing to purchases. Beyond Wellington, Sutter identifies other expensive rental markets including western Lake Worth, Delray Beach and Boca Raton. He notes that "more acreage and more land has become more popular, even when it comes down to rentals."

Rental price variations across South Florida counties reveal significant disparities. HUD data for one-bedroom apartments shows Okeechobee County at $1,032, Indian River County at $1,222, and St. Lucie/Martin areas at $1,467. Fair Market Rent calculations use surveys, rental listings and market adjustments to reflect current conditions and help determine housing assistance amounts, though the figures do not establish rent control limits. For renters seeking better deals, Sutter recommends thorough market research: "Know the market, do your comps. You have to really, really know the area if you don't want to get ripped off paying rent."

cards.headline: Sara Baxter drops congressional bid, reenters Palm Beach County Commission race after Trump post

cards.body:

Baxter said her initial run for Congress was motivated by her desire to help more people in her community. "With this new district and living in it, it was kind of one of those lifetime opportunities," Baxter said. "I want to be able to help residents and help more of them."

In a statement Thursday night, Baxter said she had spoken with Trump by phone and was grateful for his leadership. "There's more work ahead, and I'm ready to keep serving the people of Palm Beach County," she said. Trump, who had previously endorsed Baxter's commission campaign, posted that "Sara Baxter is a fantastic person, and highly qualified for many top political jobs but, on a somewhat selfish basis, I would rather have her stay on the Palm Beach County Commission (where so many important things are happening!), than run for Congress." Political analyst Brian Crowley said without Trump's endorsement for a congressional run, the race would be difficult for Baxter. Trump's statement made it less likely his endorsement for commissioner would extend to a congressional campaign, according to Crowley.

The rare flower could bloom in the next few days or weeks, according to updates from the botanical garden's Instagram account. Its bloom period typically lasts only 24 to 48 hours, during which it emits the stench of rotting flesh, hence its distinctive name. Goalkeeper Eloy Room told WPTV that the outpouring of support fueled the team's excitement. "Really joyful to see that so many people showed up today. It gives us energy. We're really excited to start the World Cup," Room said. Midfielder Tahitch Chong said the moment carries enormous meaning for both the players and the entire island. "I think it's amazing to see. I don't think the people back home are going to believe the crowd we had here. But just to see everyone, the whole world speak highly about Curaçao, just speaking highly about the island is obviously amazing," Chong said.

Curaçao, an island nation with a population of just over 150,000 people, is the smallest nation to qualify for the tournament and went undefeated in all 10 of its 2026 World Cup qualifying matches. Some Curaçao natives traveled from as far as Port St. Lucie to attend. Marionella Barzeycoggins, originally from Curaçao, said she found out about the training event in Boca and made sure to RSVP and bring her whole family. Room said the team had worked long toward this moment. "We fought long for this moment to play in the World Cup. Now we're here, we're going to show the world what we can," Room said. Curaçao faces Germany this Sunday in Houston, Texas.

hero.headline: Humane Society of the Treasure Coast uses Stuart thrift stores for animal care during Palm City shelter renovations
hero.teaser: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is using its two thrift stores to keep animal care going during a major renovation of its shelter in Palm City.
hero.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is relying on its two thrift stores to maintain animal care operations while undergoing major renovations at its Palm City shelter. The nonprofit started construction on its adoption, customer service, and intake areas earlier this year, which forced the organization to find creative solutions for housing its animals. According to spokesperson Sarah Fisher, many of the shelter's cats have been temporarily moved to the thrift store locations. Fisher emphasized how important this transition has been, noting that with their shelter cages unavailable during construction, the stores have provided essential space for the animals.

The thrift stores are now serving dual purposes for the organization. Senior Manager Kelly Ellis explained that customers shopping for unique items can also browse adoptable cats while visiting either location. This approach keeps the animals visible to potential adopters while freeing up much-needed space at the main facility. Ellis stressed that every purchase made at the thrift stores directly supports the animals in their care. The organization welcomes donations of gently used goods, which shoppers can drop off while exploring the merchandise and meeting available pets.

While the stores house some animals during construction, the Humane Society is also actively seeking temporary foster homes for other animals. This two-pronged approach allows the organization to care for its full population while the renovation project continues. The strategy demonstrates how animal shelters can adapt when buildings require upgrades, maintaining both operations and community connections during challenging transitions.

The Humane Society's thrift stores are located at 3302 SE Federal Highway in Stuart and 1099 NW 21st Street in Stuart. For more information about store hours and guidelines for donating items, visit hstc1.org.

cards.headline: Hundreds of fish found dead in Port St. Lucie community after city algae treatment
cards.teaser: Dead fish were floating in the Sawgrass Lakes community in Port St. Lucie on Thursday after the city hired a vendor to treat the water for toxic algae earlier in the week.
cards.body:
Dead fish were found floating in the Sawgrass Lakes community on Thursday morning after the city of Port St. Lucie treated the water for toxic algae on Tuesday and Wednesday. The city hired SOLitude to perform the treatment. Neighbors shared videos of hundreds of dead fish in their backyards, with resident Jim Herbert describing "hundreds and hundreds of fish here, hundreds and hundreds of those little ones just gulping the air." Experts told WPTV that high heat combined with algae treatment can make water uninhabitable for aquatic life. On Thursday, crews removed the dead fish and tested oxygen levels in the water.

Scott Samples with the city of Port St. Lucie said the city has been working with neighbors and other cities and counties to find solutions. Jim Moir, executive director of the Indian Riverkeeper, recommended the city pursue more natural approaches, including planting aquatic vegetation, reducing fertilizer use, and removing sediment that fuels algae growth. Moir stated, "We're going to end up in a cycle that we can't break unless we go back to square one and start with a natural remediation." Resident Jim Herbert noted this was at least the second fish die-off since he has lived in the neighborhood. Neighbor Jerry Cook said he does not think the issue is "an overnight fix" or "a couple months fix," but rather "a few years fix."

cards.headline: Martin County Commissioner calls for talks to move Brightline station from downtown Stuart
cards.teaser: Martin County Commissioner Ed Ciampi asked county staff to begin discussions with Brightline leadership about moving the planned train station from its previous.
cards.body:
Martin County Commissioner Ed Ciampi called on county staff to begin discussions with Brightline leadership about potentially moving the planned train station from its previously agreed-upon downtown Stuart location. Ciampi cited parking issues and other concerns with the current site, a parking lot across from the courthouse in downtown Stuart, and suggested the fairgrounds as an alternative location. His request came after the FEC sent a letter to then-Stuart mayor Christopher Collins stating it does not support a Brightline station in Stuart because the proposed station violates U.S. Coast Guard rules. The letter explained that the station would require the St. Lucie River Railroad bridge to remain down while the train stops. Ciampi said if the Army Corps of Engineers or the U.S. Coast Guard deems the downtown location too close to restricted areas, the site should be removed from consideration, but moving the station to the fairgrounds would eliminate that issue entirely.

Community members expressed mixed reactions to the proposal. Steven Vitale, owner of the Colorado Inn, questioned the move by asking why the county would build a train station people cannot walk to when most people will want to go to downtown Stuart. However, Paul Gedwed called it a well-thought-out opinion due to congestion at the proposed location. Lisa Freitas, owner of Lisa Gay Fashion, said her downtown store will benefit regardless of the station's location and urged officials to complete the project as long as it remains in Martin County. The county clarified that Ciampi's comments are not official direction for staff. The topic must return to the board for discussion and a vote before staff can take action on exploring a new location.

cards.headline: Indian River County one-bedroom apartment rent averages $1,222 in new federal data
cards.teaser: Indian River County rental costs for one-bedroom apartments averaged $1,222 according to new 2026 Fair Market Rent data from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
cards.body:
New 2026 data from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development shows substantial price variations for one-bedroom apartments across South Florida counties. Belle Glade in Palm Beach County posted the lowest rate at $890, while Wellington in Palm Beach County reached the highest at $2,850. Okeechobee County came in at $1,032, Indian River County at $1,222, and St. Lucie and Martin areas at $1,467. The ZIP code 33449 in Wellington posted even higher rates for four-bedroom homes, exceeding $5,080 monthly according to HUD data.

Real estate broker Talbot Sutter, president of Sutter and Nugent Real Estate, attributes Wellington's high costs to quality amenities and location advantages. "A lot of it has to do with school districts, especially Wellington. They have like top A-rated schools, lifestyle, they have so many aspects from equestrian to outdoor activities," Sutter said. He identifies the priciest rental markets in Wellington, western Lake Worth, Delray Beach and Boca Raton, noting that "more acreage and more land has become more popular, even when it comes down to rentals." For renters, Sutter recommends knowing the market: "Know the market, do your comps. You have to really, really know the area if you don't want to get ripped off paying rent."

cards.headline: Corpse flower nicknamed Princess Pungent set to bloom at McKee Botanical Garden in Vero Beach
cards.teaser: A rare corpse flower could bloom in the next few days or weeks at McKee Botanical Garden in Vero Beach.
cards.body:
The Titan Arum, also known as the corpse flower, is set to bloom at McKee Botanical Garden in Vero Beach in the coming days or weeks. The botanical garden has been tracking the plant's progress on Instagram under the nickname "Princess Pungent." The flower's bloom period typically lasts only 24 to 48 hours, during which it emits the stench of rotting flesh, a characteristic that inspired its common name. The plant is native to the rainforests of Sumatra and Indonesia and is considered endangered.

This Titan Arum arrived at McKee in May 2026. According to a Thursday update from the botanical garden, the flower has grown nine inches taller and one of its three remaining leaves has dropped, both signs that bloom time is approaching. McKee Botanical Garden's annual Waterlily Celebration takes place June 13, which could provide an opportunity for visitors to witness and experience the full bloom of this rare plant.

cards.headline: Lawsuit challenges Florida property tax ballot language as biased and misleading
cards.teaser: A lawsuit filed Thursday challenges the property-tax amendment Florida lawmakers recently approved for the November ballot, arguing the language is biased and misleading.
cards.body:
A lawsuit filed Thursday in Leon County challenges the ballot language for a property-tax amendment Florida lawmakers approved for the November 2026 General Election. The complaint, filed by a voter advocacy group and two registered voters, argues the ballot language is "biased" and "misleading," accusing lawmakers of using campaign-style phrases like "Save Our Homes From Excessive Property Taxes," "protecting small businesses" and "ensuring fairness." The plaintiffs contend the summary overstates the proposal by suggesting it guarantees funding for core services, fully eliminates non-school homestead taxes and immediately exempts the first $250,000 of a home's value, when the filing argues the initial exemption would be $150,000 in 2027. The lawsuit asks a judge to declare the wording unconstitutional and order Attorney General James Uthmeier to rewrite it within 10 days.

Attorney Jamie Cole, representing the plaintiffs, argues a ballot amendment should be fair, neutral and accurate. Cole successfully challenged a similar property-tax amendment in 2007, when a judge found the ballot language for a proposed "Super Exemption" misleading and ordered the measure removed from the ballot. On June 2, lawmakers passed legislation raising the homestead exemption to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. The amendment will require approval from at least 60 percent of voters to become law.

cards.headline: Fresh produce prices climb more than 6% as Treasure Coast shoppers adapt buying habits
cards.teaser: Fresh fruit and vegetable prices climbed more than 6% over the past year, according to Thursday's federal inflation report, forcing shoppers to change how they buy groceries.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County shoppers are changing their grocery habits as fresh fruit and vegetable prices climbed more than 6% over the past year, according to federal inflation data through May and a new study from financial services company Advance America. One in three American families now purchase fewer fresh fruits and vegetables due to rising costs, while 20% have switched to frozen alternatives. One Palm Beach County shopper said the quality remains the same with frozen options, noting that organic frozen produce costs about the same as fresh. Another shopper described his new strategy of shopping at multiple locations, including Don Victor's in Lake Worth for vegetables, making two or three stops on shopping day to find better deals.

The economic impact is significant for Florida residents, who now spend over $28 more monthly on groceries compared to previous periods. Federal data shows overall grocery prices increased 2.7% year-over-year through May, with fresh produce leading the increases. Not all shoppers have dramatically changed their purchasing patterns. One consumer said rising prices are manageable since shopping only for one person, and continues buying fresh produce in moderate quantities.

hero.headline: Wellington Soccer Club posts record 840 registrations as World Cup excitement builds
hero.teaser: The Wellington Soccer Club has registered more than 840 children for the upcoming season, a record turnout that coaches attribute to World Cup excitement across South Florida.
hero.body:
The Wellington Soccer Club has reached a historic milestone with more than 840 children registering for the upcoming season. Club leaders and coaches say the record turnout stems directly from growing enthusiasm around the World Cup across South Florida. At Greenview Shores Park, young players are training with professional aspirations on their minds. Nine-year-old Parker is among them, inspired by Argentinian soccer star Tadeo Allende, who currently plays for Inter Miami. "I want to be like Allende when I grow up, he's my favorite player," Parker said.

Patrick Zoete, the club's director of coaching, brings more than 25 years of experience to the sport. He emphasizes that soccer offers young players benefits far beyond physical fitness. "Soccer provides not only exercise but also a way of life for the kids to be part of a team, camaraderie. Some of them remain friends for life," Zoete explained. The Wellington Soccer Club is one of many organizations throughout the area experiencing this surge in enrollment, reflecting a broader pattern of increased interest in the sport.

Zoete confirmed that this uptick follows a predictable four-year cycle centered around the World Cup tournament. "We wait four years for a World Cup. I mean, it's huge," he said. He also noted that South Florida has a unique advantage this season with the presence of Lionel Messi at Inter Miami, which gives local fans the opportunity to watch one of the world's greatest players compete at a professional level. This combination of global tournament excitement and local star power appears to be driving families to register their children for soccer.

For the young athletes themselves, the appeal extends beyond tournament hype. Parker represents many players who return each season primarily for the social connections and competitive experience. "Spending time with my friends. I meet new people every year. Every time we have a game, I'm really excited," Parker said. Zoete reinforces this sentiment, encouraging young people to embrace the sport simply for its inherent enjoyment. "Get a ball and go play. Join a team and have fun," he said. As the World Cup approaches, the Wellington Soccer Club's record registration numbers demonstrate how major sporting events can inspire community participation and help young athletes discover a lifelong passion for soccer.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie resident travels to Boca Raton to watch Curaçao train ahead of historic World Cup debut
cards.teaser: Hundreds of soccer fans filled Florida Atlantic University stadium in Boca Raton Thursday to watch Curaçao hold a training session ahead of the team's first-eve.
cards.body:
Hundreds of soccer fans gathered at Florida Atlantic University stadium in Boca Raton on Thursday, waving jerseys and flags to witness Curaçao's training session ahead of the team's historic first-ever World Cup appearance this weekend. Goalkeeper Eloy Room told WPTV the large turnout energized the squad. "Really joyful to see that so many people showed up today — it gives us energy. We're really excited to start the World Cup," Room said. Midfielder Tahitch Chong said the global attention on the island held enormous meaning for both players and residents back home. "I think it's amazing to see. I don't think the people back home are going to believe the crowd we had here," Chong said.

Curaçao, an island nation with a population of just over 150,000 people, is the smallest nation to qualify for the tournament and went undefeated in all 10 of its 2026 World Cup qualifying matches. Fans traveled from across South Florida to attend, including Port St. Lucie resident Marionella Barzeycoggins, a Curaçao native who brought her entire family after learning about the event. Local fan Bruce Zalman said he plans to attend games at Hard Rock Stadium. Curaçao faces Germany this Sunday in Houston, Texas, in their opening match.

cards.headline: Oxbridge Academy Thunderwolves rebuild under new coach Mike Colee after winless season
cards.teaser: The Oxbridge Academy Thunderwolves are working to rebuild under new head football coach Mike Colee, who has already increased roster numbers in his first few weeks on the job.
cards.body:
The Oxbridge Academy Thunderwolves are rebuilding under newly named head football coach Mike Colee, who has already begun reshaping the program just weeks into his position. Initial roster numbers were lower at the start because many players had already made summer plans before Colee's involvement. However, after meeting with parents and players and releasing the schedule, the numbers have grown. Senior Cayden Pribramski said Colee emphasizes mental toughness and builds the system around individual player strengths rather than imposing a rigid approach. "He's not the kind of guy to go out there and say, 'my way or the highway,'" Pribramski said. "He's going to really build the stuff around you and help you to succeed."

The Thunderwolves are working to move past last year's 0-11 season. Senior Brady Basis said the team is focused on maintaining momentum after a spring win. "We just want to keep working, keep going," Basis said. "We came off a good spring win. Keep bringing that energy and build it in the next season." Players said Colee's coaching style is already resonating with the team and could be instrumental in the program's future success.

cards.headline: Humane Society of the Treasure Coast uses Stuart thrift stores to house cats during Palm City shelter renovation
cards.teaser: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is using its two Stuart thrift stores to house cats while its Palm City shelter undergoes major renovations.
cards.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is using its two thrift stores to house cats while its Palm City shelter undergoes a major renovation. According to spokesperson Sarah Fisher, the nonprofit began construction on its adoption, customer service, and intake areas earlier this year, temporarily relocating many of its cats to the store locations. Fisher explained that with shelter cages unavailable during the renovation, the stores have become essential for animal care. Senior Manager Kelly Ellis noted that shoppers can now find both unique items for sale and adoptable cats at both thrift stores, with donations of gently used goods helping to support the animals.

The Humane Society's thrift stores are located at 3302 SE Federal Highway in Stuart and 1099 NW 21st St, Stuart. The organization is currently seeking temporary foster homes for other animals while construction continues. Store hours and donation guidelines are available at hstc1.org.

cards.teaser: A rare Titan Arum, nicknamed Princess Pungent, could bloom in the next few days or weeks at McKee Botanical Garden in Vero Beach.

The corpse flower, scientifically known as Titan Arum, is set to bloom soon at McKee Botanical Garden in Vero Beach. During its bloom period, which typically lasts only 24 to 48 hours, the flower emits the stench of rotting flesh, which is how it earned its common name. The plant is native to the rainforests of Sumatra and Indonesia and is considered endangered.

McKee Botanical Garden's Titan Arum arrived at the facility in May 2026. According to a Thursday update from the garden's Instagram, the flower has already grown nine inches taller, and one of three remaining leaves has dropped, signs that bloom time is approaching. cards.headline: Singer Island beach littered with trash, overflowing cans after Memorial Day weekend
cards.teaser: Overflowing trash cans, glass tequila bottles, styrofoam cups and beer cans were found on Singer Island beach just feet away from sea turtle nests after Memorial Day weekend.
cards.body:
Singer Island's beach was found littered with overflowing trash cans, glass tequila bottles, styrofoam cups and beer cans following the Memorial Day weekend, with some debris located just feet away from sea turtle nests. Beachgoer Stacie Safford expressed concern for the environment and sea turtles nesting nearby. The city of Riviera Beach said in a statement that beach activity increased significantly over the holiday weekend near Johnny Longboats, resulting in more trash than usual. Parks and Recreation staff worked throughout the weekend to maintain the beach and surrounding public areas, with beach maintenance scheduled from 7 a.m. over the weekend and 6:30 a.m. on Memorial Day.

To support the holiday crowds, the city increased beach restroom cleanings to three times during the weekend, including Monday, up from the usual two weekend cleanings. Daily assignments included opening restrooms, emptying trash receptacles, clearing sand from showers, sidewalks, pavilions and playgrounds, and servicing trash cans along beach access points. Oceanside Beach Services assists with upkeep in designated service areas, including trash removal and seaweed clearing. The city noted that during turtle season, sifting and combing are permitted only in limited beach areas to help protect sea turtle nests. Safford said she hopes visitors will be more mindful and take their trash with them, even if cans are full.

hero.headline: Delray Beach Public Library offers free summer STREAM programs and daily meals for Florida youth
hero.teaser: The Delray Beach Public Library is running free STREAM programs for kids and teens this summer, including art history sessions, 3D puzzles, and hands-on archaeology activities, along with free daily lunches and snacks.
hero.body:
The Delray Beach Public Library is making summer brighter for kids and teens with free STREAM programs—Science, Technology, Reading, Art, Engineering and Math—open to all Florida residents. According to Kae Jonsons, director of development and community relations, the library has been serving the community since 1913, when 30 women from the Ladies Improvement Society each donated a book to start the collection. Today, it welcomes more than 193,000 visitors annually to its 36,000-square-foot facility at Atlantic Avenue and Swinton Avenue.

Young adult librarian Natalie Baron is leading sessions like ColorSpace: Artistic Excavations, where teens explore art history from cave paintings to ancient pottery. Teens can also join lab-based activities including collaborative 3D puzzle builds and pick up themed book boxes. Mandy Fulop, head of the children's department, is launching the STREAM Into Summer Literacy Program, encouraging young readers to set goals with librarians, track progress, and take home an Unearth a Story bag with a free STREAM book and activities. In partnership with the School District of Palm Beach County, the library serves free lunch daily from 11:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. and snacks from 2 p.m. to 4 p.m. to youth up to 18. Family Nights on select Tuesdays invite children 5 and older to explore STREAM topics together. A full program lineup is available at delraylibrary.org.

cards.headline: Cornell Art Museum in Delray Beach debuts upcycled art exhibition through September
cards.teaser: The Cornell Art Museum at Old School Square has opened Persistence of Matter, a summer exhibition featuring artists who transform discarded materials into sculptures and installations.
cards.body:
The Cornell Art Museum at Old School Square has opened its newest summer exhibition, Persistence of Matter, spotlighting artists who turn discarded materials into striking works of art. According to Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority Cultural Arts Director Marusca Gatto, the show underscores the museum's mission to marry creativity with community impact. Guest curators Mavis Benson and Pamela Lambie have selected artists whose sculptures, installations, and mixed media pieces are all crafted from reclaimed objects. Featured creators include Autumn Kioti, whose work draws on natural and urban influences, and Mike Silverman, whose Self-Reflection series uses discarded hard drive platters and printed circuit boards to create reflective sculptures.

"Every piece invites viewers to see themselves and their relationship to technology and waste in a new light," Silverman said. As communities face growing concerns about sustainability, Persistence of Matter offers an artistic reminder of the enduring life cycles of the materials we discard. The exhibition runs through September 10, 2026, with special programs including artist talks, salon discussions, and film screenings. Museum hours are Wednesday from noon to 5 p.m., Thursday and Friday from noon to 7 p.m., Saturday from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., and Sunday from noon to 5 p.m. For event details, call 561-654-2220.

hero.headline: Police union backs Paul Renner while gun rights group endorses Byron Donalds in Florida Governor's race
hero.body:
As the August 18 primary election approaches, two leading Republican candidates for governor are touting endorsements from powerful interest groups. The Florida Fraternal Order of Police has thrown its support behind former House Speaker Paul Renner, citing his prosecutorial background and commitment to public safety. Meanwhile, Gun Owners of America has endorsed U.S. Representative Byron Donalds for his strong stance on Second Amendment rights.

Corey Logan, President of the Florida Fraternal Order of Police, explained that Renner stands out as the clear choice for the endorsement. According to Logan, Renner has consistently shown that law and order serves as the foundation for successful communities. The FOP president stated that Renner has earned the trust of Florida law enforcement by fighting for policies that strengthen public safety, protect officers, support victims, and uphold the rule of law. Renner, a Palm Coast resident, expressed his honor at receiving the endorsement, which he considers among the most significant in the race. He pledged to continue backing law enforcement as governor and to ensure officers receive the support they deserve. The endorsement arrives as Renner faces fundraising challenges, having raised just over $100,000 in April and May while trailing in polls. However, Renner maintains that informal straw polls among close observers of the race favor him.

Donalds has accumulated multiple national endorsements, with Gun Owners of America's backing being the most recent. The group praised Donalds as a champion for the Second Amendment in Congress who has fought against gun control measures. Former state Representative Jamie Grant, who served alongside Donalds in the legislature, highlighted his colleague's record on gun rights. During the heated debate following the 2018 Parkland school shooting, Donalds was one of very few Republicans who voted against what Grant called the most intense and emotional gun control bill in Florida's modern history. Grant noted that despite intense pressure from Republican leadership to pass legislation, Donalds held firm in his opposition while still expressing commitment to school safety.

The legislation in question was the Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School Public Safety Act, which raised the minimum age for rifle purchases to 21, established a three-day waiting period for gun purchases, and banned bump stocks. The law also created a school guardian program that has since been expanded. Donalds' uncompromising stance on this measure distinguishes him from other candidates in the race, according to Grant, who argued that his former colleague successfully balanced school safety concerns with protection of individual liberties.

cards.headline: Tampa Bay NOW joins calls to cancel Ye concerts at Raymond James Stadium over antisemitic statements
cards.teaser: Tampa Bay NOW is calling for the cancellation of Ye's upcoming concerts at Raymond James Stadium, joining U.S. Sen. Rick Scott and Jewish community advocates expressing concern about the artist's scheduled Tampa performances.
cards.body:
Tampa Bay NOW is calling for the cancellation of Ye's upcoming concerts at Raymond James Stadium on June 26 and June 28, joining U.S. Senator Rick Scott and Jewish community advocates. In a press release Thursday, Tampa Bay NOW urged the Tampa Sports Authority Board, Hillsborough County Commissioners, state lawmakers, Raymond James Stadium and local officials to "immediately cancel all support for this concert." The group highlighted Ye's history of antisemitic comments, including praise for Adolf Hitler and promotion of antisemitic conspiracy theories. Tampa Bay NOW stated that "providing a prominent stage to someone whose words have repeatedly fueled antisemitism is unacceptable" and argued that allowing the concerts to move forward would send the wrong message at a time of heightened concern over antisemitism.

Scott's letter to the Tampa Sports Authority Board urged the Board not to "platform a hateful person pushing evil ideologies" using taxpayer money, writing that Ye's antisemitic comments are "an affront to the values of the people of the Hillsborough community." Scott also pointed to Ye's 2025 Super Bowl ad directing viewers to merchandise featuring swastikas, calling his remarks "vile and a slap in the face" to Florida's Jewish community. Tampa Sports Authority Chair Patrick Manteiga told Florida Politics that Scott's letter was followed by a surge of public emails. Manteiga said canceling the contract based solely on objections to Ye's statements could expose the authority to legal risk, noting the authority is close to selling out 100,000 tickets. The Jewish Community Relations Council of the Jewish Federation of Florida's Gulf Coast has also urged community members to contact local leaders about the concerts.

cards.headline: Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia blasts Miami-Dade County for $470 million in wasteful spending
cards.teaser: Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia held a news conference in Miami Thursday taking aim at what he described as the local government's increasingly unnecessary spending, the second time in the past year he has targeted Miami-Dade County.
cards.body:
Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia held a news conference in Miami Thursday to blast the county for "excessive, wasteful spending," marking the second time in a year he has targeted Miami-Dade's budget practices. Ingoglia said unnecessary spending increased to $470 million in the 2025-2026 fiscal year budget, up from his October estimate of $300 million. He pointed out that over the last three years, Miami-Dade has excessively and wastefully spent more than $800 million in taxpayer funds. The CFO noted that while Miami-Dade increased its budget by $1.08 billion since 2019, the county added only 154,248 new residents in approximately the same period, demonstrating that budget growth has far outpaced population growth.

Ingoglia used the opportunity to advocate for a referendum scheduled for November that would reduce the state's homestead exemption tax. The measure requires 60 percent voter approval to be enacted and was sent to referendum after the Florida Legislature approved it during a Special Session that concluded last week. Governor Ron DeSantis, who has prioritized property tax relief, signed the legislation. Ingoglia has targeted approximately two dozen local governments over the past year for overtaxing and wasteful spending, identifying roughly $2.7 billion in wasteful spending since beginning his crusade in 2025. On Monday, he said Jacksonville has escalated its wasteful spending.

cards.headline: North Miami lawmaker Dotie Joseph files to challenge David Jolly in Democratic Governor's Primary
cards.teaser: North Miami lawmaker Dotie Joseph quietly filed to run for Governor on Thursday, giving Democrats another candidate alongside former U.S. Rep. David Jolly as qualifying week continues.
cards.body:
North Miami lawmaker Dotie Joseph filed to run in the Democratic gubernatorial primary, joining former U.S. Congressman David Jolly in the race. Joseph's entry was unexpected, particularly given Jolly's significant fundraising advantage and status as the party's clear front-runner. Jolly has raised more than $6.1 million compared to the sub-$11,000 total Joseph has accumulated over the past two years.

The Republican primary field continued to expand when Lt. Gov. Jay Collins officially qualified on Thursday, joining fellow GOP contenders Byron Donalds, Paul Renner and James Fishback on the ballot. In the Attorney General race, former state Sen. Jose Javier Rodriguez and appointed incumbent Attorney General James Uthmeier remain the only two candidates. Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson picked up a Democratic challenger when Don Pritchard paid the qualifying fee, ensuring the incumbent won't win outright with a victory in the Aug. 18 primary. Qualifying week ends Friday at noon.

cards.headline: Rep. Randy Fine cancels appearance at Florida GOP event after James Fishback announced as speaker
cards.teaser: Randy Fine canceled an appearance at a Republican Party of Florida event after officials announced Governor candidate James Fishback will speak at the Sunshine State Showdown.
cards.body:
Rep. Randy Fine canceled his appearance at the Republican Party of Florida's Sunshine State Showdown after officials announced Governor candidate James Fishback would speak at the event. Fine had been scheduled as a featured guest before party officials unveiled an expanded guest list Thursday that included several gubernatorial candidates, including Fishback, who has made openly racist attacks against frontrunner Byron Donalds. "I have canceled my appearance at this event," Fine posted on X. "If the Florida GOP wants to host a Neo-Nazi rally, they will do it without me." Fine is Jewish.

Fishback and Fine have a history of public and personal conflicts. Earlier this year, Fishback denied entry to Jewish students at a University of South Florida event. When asked about Fine's cancellation, Fishback texted Florida Politics: "Good riddance." Fine endorsed Donalds, whom Fishback has repeatedly called "Byrone" and labeled a "DEI Hire" despite Donalds winning multiple congressional elections and leading Republican primary polls. Fine previously canceled an appearance with the Heritage Foundation after leaders refused to distance themselves from white nationalist Nick Fuentes, whom Fishback has praised. Fine has called Tucker Carlson, who interviewed Fishback about Fine's pro-Israel positions, the "most dangerous antisemite" in the country. The expanded Sunshine State Showdown speaker list also includes Lt. Jay Collins, former state House Speaker Paul Renner, and hunter Bobby Williams.

cards.headline: Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick qualifies to make comeback run in Floridas 20th Congressional District
cards.teaser: Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick is now officially running to reclaim her old seat in Congress after paying a $10,440 fee to get on the ballot in Florida's 20th Congressional District.
cards.body:
Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick is now officially running to reclaim her old seat in Congress after paying a $10,440 fee to get on the ballot in Florida's 20th Congressional District. She will face strong competition, including U.S. Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz. Her entry makes it harder for Black candidates in CD 20 to unite behind one person. Progressive activist Elijah Manning has already qualified for the race. Luther Campbell, the rapper-turned-community leader, paid the fee and shared a video on X of himself turning in his paperwork. Former Broward County Mayor Dale Holness submitted petitions to skip the fee and just needs to finish his paperwork.

hero.headline: St. Lucie and Martin areas rental costs reach $1,467 for one-bedroom apartments
hero.teaser: The St. Lucie and Martin areas show Fair Market Rent at $1,467 for one-bedroom apartments according to new HUD data.
hero.body:
According to 2026 data from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, rental prices across South Florida show dramatic variations depending on location. However, these figures represent just one snapshot of a much broader housing landscape. Wellington in Palm Beach County leads the region with the highest Fair Market Rent at nearly $2,850 for a one-bedroom, while Belle Glade offers the most affordable option in Palm Beach County at $890. Indian River County falls between these extremes at $1,222, and Okeechobee County comes in at $1,032 for comparable housing.

Real estate broker Talbot Sutter, president of Sutter and Nugent Real Estate, attributes Wellington's premium pricing to multiple factors beyond location alone. "A lot of it has to do with school districts, especially Wellington. They have like top A-rated schools, lifestyle — they have so many aspects from equestrian to outdoor activities," Sutter explained. The demand for larger properties in Wellington has also increased rental costs significantly. "More acreage and more land has become more popular, even when it comes down to rentals," Sutter said, noting that four-bedroom homes in Wellington's ZIP code 33449 exceed $5,080 monthly.

Residents across the region struggle with the rapid escalation of housing costs. Luis Rivera, who lives in Section 8 housing in Palm Beach County, describes the market plainly: "It's not easy here." He recounted seeing rental prices over two to three thousand dollars in neighborhoods that did not justify the expense. "When I first came down here rent prices were normal. And now it's like they're pushing us out," Rivera said. Joanne Bromfield, who recently relocated from Tampa after a 12-year education career to pursue real estate opportunities, found the Palm Beach County market shocking. "We literally just walked away from signing a lease like 5 minutes ago. Expensive… very expensive," she said.

HUD's Fair Market Rent figures reflect current market conditions based on similar properties in each area, using surveys, rental listings and market adjustments. These numbers help determine housing assistance programs but do not establish rent control limits for landlords. For those navigating these challenging markets, Sutter recommends thorough preparation: "Know the market, do your comps. You have to really, really know the area if you don't want to get ripped off paying rent." cards.headline: Hundreds of fish die in Port St. Lucie after city algae treatment at Sawgrass Lakes
cards.teaser: Dead fish were floating in the Sawgrass Lakes community Thursday after the city hired a vendor to treat toxic algae earlier in the week.
cards.body:

Neighbors reached out to WPTV, sharing video they took of dead fish they found in their backyards Thursday morning. "There were hundreds and hundreds of fish here, hundreds and hundreds of those little ones just gulping the air," said neighbor Jim Herbert. On Tuesday and Wednesday, the city hired a vendor, SOLitude, to treat the water for toxic algae. Experts told WPTV that with high heat and algae treatment, the water can become uninhabitable for aquatic life. On Thursday, crews were in the neighborhood removing the dead fish and testing the oxygen levels in the water. cards.headline: Wrongful death lawsuit filed in fatal Florida Turnpike crash involving semi in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: A lawsuit was filed Thursday after a fatal crash on Florida's Turnpike that killed three people when a semi-truck driver made an illegal U-turn in St. Lucie County.
cards.body:
A wrongful death lawsuit was filed Thursday months after a fatal crash on Florida's Turnpike killed three people when commercial truck driver Harjinder Singh attempted an illegal U-turn in St. Lucie County. The lawsuit, filed by an attorney representing the estate of victim Faniola Joseph, names multiple defendants including Singh, trucking company White Hawk Carriers Inc., freight broker C.H. Robinson Company Inc., and company manager Harpreet Singh. On Aug. 12, 2025, at approximately 2:57 p.m., Singh attempted an illegal U-turn through a median crossover on Florida's Turnpike near Mile Marker 171. The crossover was clearly marked "U-TURN OFFICIAL USE ONLY," court documents state. The 53-foot trailer swung across and completely blocked all northbound travel lanes. A minivan driven by Herby Dufresne, carrying passengers Rodrigue Dor and Faniola Joseph, struck the left side of the trailer in what the complaint describes as "a classic and fatal underride crash." All three occupants were killed, with Joseph pronounced dead at the scene.

The lawsuit alleges White Hawk Carriers had a documented unsafe federal safety record before C.H. Robinson selected the company to transport the load. The complaint alleges this record included a prior reportable crash on approximately Dec. 9, 2024, multiple roadside inspection citations for unsafe driving violations including speeding and improper lane changes, repeated hours-of-service violations with falsified duty status records, and vehicle defects including brake problems and air-brake leaks. The lawsuit seeks damages exceeding $75,000 under Florida's Wrongful Death Act.

hero.headline: Sawgrass Lakes residents call for natural solutions after Port St. Lucie fish kill

hero.body:

The 5 O'Clock Somewhere Fest takes over downtown West Palm Beach this Friday and Saturday, bringing an expected 10,000 to 15,000 festival-goers each day for a total attendance around 30,000. The two-day festival features live music performances from Ella Langley, Old Dominion, Jimmy Buffett's Coral Reefer Band and more, along with a behind-the-scenes experience with songwriters. Temple Ricke with Peachtree Entertainment said the festival blends live music, coastal culture and hospitality, with the main goal to drive revenue in West Palm Beach and make it a community event. West Palm Beach was chosen as the location because Alan Jackson shot his "5 O'Clock Somewhere" music video with Jimmy Buffett there. Organizers have spent about a year building relationships with the city of West Palm Beach, Discover the Palm Beaches, local vendors and law enforcement.

Several roads in downtown West Palm Beach will be closed through Wednesday, June 17. Flagler Drive from Fern Street to Banyan Boulevard, the 100 blocks of North and South Clematis Streets, and the 100 blocks of Evernia Street and Datura Street will all be closed. The official kickoff party is a free pre-party at the Square Grouper with doors opening at 7 p.m. Thursday, featuring an Alan Jackson look-alike contest where participants can win VIP festival tickets. Cowboy Club is hosting the official after party Saturday night.

cards.headline: Wellington Soccer Club reports record 840 registrations as World Cup excitement builds
cards.teaser: More than 840 children have registered to play with the Wellington Soccer Club for the upcoming season, a record turnout that coaches attribute to growing World Cup excitement.
cards.body:
The Wellington Soccer Club is experiencing record growth with more than 840 children registered for the upcoming season, a surge organizers attribute to World Cup excitement across South Florida. At Greenview Shores Park, boys and girls are training with aspirations of reaching soccer's biggest stage. Patrick Zoete, the club's director of coaching, has taught soccer for more than 25 years and said the surge follows a pattern that repeats every four years around the World Cup. He noted that South Florida is fortunate to have Lionel Messi playing at Inter Miami, allowing fans to watch the best player in the world.

For 9-year-old Parker, the dreams of professional soccer are already forming. Parker said he wants to be like Argentinian soccer star Tadeo Allende, who now plays for Inter Miami. According to Zoete, soccer offers young players far more than athletic development. "Soccer provides not only exercise but also a way of life for the kids to be part of a team, camaraderie. Some of them remain friends for life," Zoete said. Parker said what keeps him returning each season is spending time with friends and meeting new people, adding that he gets excited before every game.
